This app respects your privacy. Below is a list of data the app may access and how it is used. All data is stored locally on your device and is never uploaded to any server.
Access Bluetooth to scan and connect heart rate monitor devices. Reads device name and MAC address (for device identification and auto-reconnect only). No other device info is collected.
Reads real-time heart rate and RR intervals, saves to local database for history and statistics. Data stays on this device and is never uploaded.
Optional feature to record exercise trajectory correlated with heart rate. Disabled by default; requires manual permission and enablement. Data stored locally only.
Saves heart rate history and settings to local database and files, ensuring data persists after app closure.
Sends notifications when heart rate exceeds preset thresholds or device disconnects, helping you monitor health status.
Used for app update checks and repository access; optional HTTP/WebSocket server and webhook push features also use network. No personal data is uploaded.
Uses foreground service for continuous heart rate monitoring in background, ensuring data recording continues when screen is off, with a persistent notification.

Fair Memory is an Android memory management specification jointly advocated by GSA board members (vivo, Xiaomi, OPPO, Honor). It aims to let apps proactively cooperate with the system to release resources through standardized system broadcasts when memory is tight, thereby improving overall device performance and stability, and reducing the probability of background apps being force-killed.

When system memory resources are tight, the device ROM sends specific broadcast notifications to registered apps. Upon receiving the broadcast, apps can perform corresponding memory optimization operations based on the broadcast type, including releasing non-critical caches, stopping low-priority tasks, saving current state, etc. This proactive approach is smoother than the system directly killing processes, effectively reducing the experience interruption caused by app restarts.

Action: itgsa.intent.action.TRIM\nSent when system memory is tight. Upon receiving this, apps should proactively release non-critical memory, such as clearing image caches, stopping non-essential background tasks, triggering garbage collection, etc.

Action: itgsa.intent.action.KILL\nSent when the system is about to kill this app. Upon receiving this, apps should save critical state data, release all releasable resources, and prepare for process termination.

This app has been adapted to the Fair Memory mechanism according to GSA official documentation:
• Dynamically register broadcast receivers at Application startup with RECEIVER_EXPORTED flag • Parse common and extra Bundles from Intent, extracting anomaly type (physical memory/Java heap), memory usage, callback IBinder info • TRIM broadcast: differentiated release by notifyType — physical memory anomaly (1000) clears entire chart cache, Java heap anomaly (2000) downsamples to keep latest 500 points; both clear scan results and trigger System.gc(), notify system via IBinder callback within 3 seconds • TRIM foreground notification: when the app is in the foreground and reaches kill conditions, proactively push notifications to remind users. Java heap anomalies provide \"Close App\" and \"Ignore\" options; physical memory anomalies provide \"Reopen\" • KILL broadcast: notify MainViewModel to save state (heart rate data already persisted via Room database), notify system via IBinder callback within 3 seconds • Delegate release logic to MainViewModel via MemoryListener interface (WeakReference) to prevent memory leaks • Implement IBinder.DeathRecipient to monitor system service abnormal death • Use dedicated HandlerThread for broadcast processing to avoid blocking main thread
BLE heart rate service (BleService) runs as a foreground service and won\'t be interrupted by memory warnings. Status bar resident service and floating window service may be reclaimed by the system under extreme memory pressure; the app will auto-recover on next launch.
